chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abdullah al-Kinanī from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī from al-Ḥasan ibn Hārūn said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): I am fond of my beard, and while I am in iḥrām, the hairs fall out. He said: 'When you finish your iḥrām, buy dates with a dirham and give them in charity, for one date is better than one hair.' And whoever plucks both of his armpits completely, a sheep is obligatory upon him, according to what we have previously mentioned in the report of Zurārah from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him), and also what he narrated.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or ʿUmrah
key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: A silver coin used as a unit of currency
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation or compensation for violating a ritual rule

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for accidentally losing beard hair while in the state of iḥrām during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific expiation (kaffārah) for unintentional hair loss during iḥrām, establishing a symbolic equivalence where one date outweighs one hair in merit. It further clarifies the penalty for plucking both armpits entirely, linking it to the precedent set by Zurarah regarding the obligation of sacrificing a sheep, thereby illustrating the graduated nature of penalties for minor ritual infractions.
